vsm1.7:1.1: Now, ten recollections were listed next after the ten kinds of foulness (III.105).
vsm1.7:1.2: As to these: Mindfulness (sati) itself is recollection (anussati) because it arises again and again;
vsm1.7:1.3:
or alternatively, the mindfulness (sati) that is proper (anurūpa) for a clansman gone forth out of faith,
since it occurs only in those instances where it should occur, is “recollection” (anussati).
vsm1.7:1.4: The recollection arisen inspired by the Enlightened One is the recollection of the Buddha.
vsm1.7:1.5: This is a term for mindfulness with the Enlightened One’s special qualities as its object.
vsm1.7:1.6: The recollection arisen inspired by the Law is the recollection of the Dhamma.
vsm1.7:1.7: This is a term for mindfulness with the special qualities of the Law’s being well proclaimed, etc., as its object.
vsm1.7:1.8: The recollection arisen inspired by the Community is the recollection of the Saṅgha.
vsm1.7:1.9: This is a term for mindfulness with the Community’s special qualities of being entered on the good way, etc., as its object.
vsm1.7:1.10: The recollection arisen inspired by virtue is the recollection of virtue.
vsm1.7:1.11: This is a term for mindfulness with the special qualities of virtue’s untornness, etc., as its object.
vsm1.7:1.12: The recollection arisen inspired by generosity is the recollection of generosity.
vsm1.7:1.13: This is a term for mindfulness with generosity’s special qualities of free generosity, etc., as its object.
vsm1.7:1.14: The recollection arisen inspired by deities is the recollection of deities.
vsm1.7:1.15:
This is a term for mindfulness with the special qualities of one’s own faith,
etc., as its object with deities standing as witnesses.
vsm1.7:1.16: The recollection arisen inspired by death is the recollection of death.
vsm1.7:1.17: This is a term for mindfulness with the termination of the life faculty as its object.
vsm1.7:1.18:
Mindfulness occupied with the body (kāya-gatā sati—lit. “body-gone mindfulness”): it is gone (gata) to the material body
(kāya) that is analyzed into head hairs, etc., or it is gone into the body, thus it is “body-gone” (kāya-gatā).
vsm1.7:1.19: It is body-gone (kāya-gatā) and it is mindfulness (sati), thus it is “body-gone-mindfulness” (kāyagatasati—single compound);
vsm1.7:1.20: but instead of shortening the vowel thus in the usual way, “body-gone mindfulness” (kāyagatā sati— compound adj. + noun) is said.
vsm1.7:1.21: This is a term for mindfulness that has as its object the sign of the bodily parts consisting of head hairs and the rest.
vsm1.7:1.22: The mindfulness arisen inspired by breathing (ānāpāna) is mindfulness of breathing.
vsm1.7:1.23: This is a term for mindfulness that has as its object the sign of in-breaths and out-breaths.
vsm1.7:1.24: The recollection arisen inspired by peace is the recollection of peace.
vsm1.7:1.25: This is a term that has as its object the stilling of all suffering.
vsm1.7:2.1: Now, a meditator with absolute confidence who wants to develop firstly the recollection of the Enlightened One among these ten
vsm1.7:2.2: should go into solitary retreat in a favourable abode
vsm1.7:2.3:
and recollect the special qualities of the Enlightened One, the Blessed One, as follows: That Blessed One is such since
he is accomplished, fully enlightened, endowed with clear vision and virtuous conduct, sublime, the knower of worlds,
the incomparable leader of men to be tamed, the teacher of gods and men, enlightened and blessed (M I 37; A III 285).
vsm1.7:3.1: Here is the way he recollects:
vsm1.7:3.2: “That Blessed One is such since he is accomplished, he is such since he is fully enlightened, … he is such since he is blessed”—
vsm1.7:3.3: he is so for these several reasons, is what is meant.
vsm1.7:4.1:
Herein, what he recollects firstly is that the Blessed One is accomplished (arahanta) for the following reasons:
(i) because of remoteness (āraka), and (ii) because of his enemies (ari) and (iii) the spokes (ara) having been destroyed
(hata), and (iv) because of his worthiness (araha) of requisites, etc., and (v) because of absence of secret (rahābhāva) evil-doing.
vsm1.7:5.1: (i) He stands utterly remote and far away from all defilements
vsm1.7:5.2: because he has expunged all trace of defilement by means of the path—
vsm1.7:5.3: because of such remoteness (āraka) he is accomplished (arahanta).
vsm1.7:5.4:
A man remote (āraka) indeed we call
From something he has not at all;
vsm1.7:5.5:
The Saviour too that has no stain
May well the name “accomplished” (arahanta) gain.
vsm1.7:6.1:
(ii) And these enemies (ari), these defilements, are destroyed (hata) by the path—because
the enemies are thus destroyed he is accomplished (arahanta) also.
vsm1.7:6.2:
The enemies (ari) that were deployed,
Greed and the rest, have been destroyed (hata)
vsm1.7:6.3:
By his, the Helper’s, wisdom’s sword,
So he is “accomplished” (arahanta), all accord.
vsm1.7:7.1:
(iii) Now, this wheel of the round of rebirths with its hub made of ignorance and of craving for becoming, with its spokes
consisting of formations of merit and the rest, with its rim of ageing and death,
vsm1.7:7.2: which is joined to the chariot of the triple becoming by piercing it with the axle made of the origins of cankers (see M I 55),
vsm1.7:7.3: has been revolving throughout time that has no beginning.
vsm1.7:7.4:
All of this wheel’s spokes (ara) were destroyed (hata) by him at the Place of Enlightenment, as he stood
firm with the feet of energy on the ground of virtue, wielding with the hand of faith the axe of knowledge that destroys kamma—
vsm1.7:7.5: because the spokes are thus destroyed he is accomplished (arahanta) also.
vsm1.7:8.1: Or alternatively, it is the beginningless round of rebirths that is called the “wheel of the round of rebirths.”
vsm1.7:8.2: Ignorance is its hub because it is its root.
vsm1.7:8.3: Ageing-and-death is its rim because it terminates it.
vsm1.7:8.4:
The remaining ten states of the dependent origination are its spokes because ignorance
is their root and ageing-and-death their termination.
vsm1.7:9.1: Herein, ignorance is unknowing about suffering and the rest.
vsm1.7:9.2: And ignorance in sensual becoming is a condition for formations in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:9.3: Ignorance in fine-material becoming is a condition for formations in fine-material becoming.
vsm1.7:9.4: Ignorance in immaterial becoming is a condition for formations in immaterial becoming.
vsm1.7:10.1: Formations in sensual becoming are a condition for rebirth-linking consciousness in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:11.1: Rebirth-linking consciousness in sensual becoming is a condition for mentality-materiality in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:11.3: In immaterial becoming it is a condition for mentality only.
vsm1.7:12.1: Mentality-materiality in sensual becoming is a condition for the sixfold base in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:12.2: Mentality-materiality in fine-material becoming is a condition for three bases in fine-material becoming.
vsm1.7:12.3: Mentality in immaterial becoming is a condition for one base in immaterial becoming.
vsm1.7:13.1: The sixfold base in sensual becoming is a condition for six kinds of contact in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:13.2: Three bases in fine-material becoming are conditions for three kinds of contact in fine-material becoming.
vsm1.7:13.3: The mind base alone in immaterial becoming is a condition for one kind of contact in immaterial becoming.
vsm1.7:14.1: The six kinds of contact in sensual becoming are conditions for six kinds of feeling in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:14.2: Three kinds of contact in fine-material becoming are conditions for three kinds of feeling there too.
vsm1.7:14.3: One kind of contact in immaterial becoming is a condition for one kind of feeling there too.
vsm1.7:15.1: The six kinds of feeling in sensual becoming are conditions for the six groups of craving in sensual becoming.
vsm1.7:15.2: Three in the fine-material becoming are for three there too.
vsm1.7:15.3: One kind of feeling in the immaterial becoming is a condition for one group of craving in the immaterial becoming.
vsm1.7:15.4: The craving in the several kinds of becoming is a condition for the clinging there.
vsm1.7:16.1: Clinging, etc., are the respective conditions for becoming and the rest.
vsm1.7:16.3: Here someone thinks, “I shall enjoy sense desires,” and with sense-desire clinging as condition
vsm1.7:16.4: he misconducts himself in body, speech, and mind.
vsm1.7:16.5: Owing to the fulfilment of his misconduct he reappears in a state of loss (deprivation).
vsm1.7:16.6: The kamma that is the cause of his reappearance there is kamma-process becoming,
vsm1.7:16.7: the aggregates generated by the kamma are rebirth-process becoming,
vsm1.7:16.8: the generating of the aggregates is birth,
vsm1.7:16.9: their maturing is ageing, their dissolution is death.
vsm1.7:17.1: Another thinks, “I shall enjoy the delights of heaven,” and in the parallel manner he conducts himself well.
vsm1.7:17.2: Owing to the fulfilment of his good conduct he reappears in a sensual-sphere heaven.
vsm1.7:17.3: The kamma that is the cause of his reappearance there is kamma-process becoming, and the rest as before.
vsm1.7:18.1: Another thinks, “I shall enjoy the delights of the Brahmā-world,”
vsm1.7:18.2: and with sense-desire clinging as condition he develops loving-kindness, compassion, gladness, and equanimity.
vsm1.7:18.3: Owing to the fulfilment of the meditative development he is reborn in the Brahmā-world.
vsm1.7:18.4: The kamma that is the cause of his rebirth there is kamma-process becoming, and the rest is as before.
vsm1.7:19.1: Yet another thinks, “I shall enjoy the delights of immaterial becoming,”
vsm1.7:19.2: and with the same condition he develops the attainments beginning with the base consisting of boundless space.
vsm1.7:19.3: Owing to the fulfilment of the development he is reborn in one of these states.
vsm1.7:19.4: The kamma that is the cause of his rebirth there is kamma-process becoming,
vsm1.7:19.5: the aggregates generated by the kamma are rebirth-process becoming,
vsm1.7:19.6: the generating of the aggregates is birth,
vsm1.7:19.7: their maturing is ageing, their dissolution is death (see M II 263).
vsm1.7:19.8: The remaining kinds of clinging are construable in the same way.
vsm1.7:20.1:
So, “Understanding of discernment of conditions thus, ‘Ignorance is a cause, formations are causally
arisen, and both these states are causally arisen,’ is knowledge of the causal relationship of states.
vsm1.7:20.2:
Understanding of discernment of conditions thus, ‘In the past and in the future ignorance is a cause, formations are causally
arisen, and both these states are causally arisen,’ is knowledge of the causal relationship of states” (Paṭis I 50),
vsm1.7:20.3: and all the clauses should be given in detail in this way.
vsm1.7:21.1: Herein, ignorance and formations are one summarization;
vsm1.7:21.2: consciousness, mentality-materiality, the sixfold base, contact, and feeling are another;
vsm1.7:21.3: craving, clinging, and becoming are another;
vsm1.7:21.4: and birth and ageing-and-death are another.
vsm1.7:21.5: Here the first summarization is past, the two middle ones are present, and birth and ageing-and-death are future.
vsm1.7:22.1:
Now, the Blessed One knew, saw, understood, and penetrated in all aspects this dependent origination with its four
summarizations, its three times, its twenty aspects, and its three links.
vsm1.7:22.2: “Knowledge is in the sense of that being known,
vsm1.7:22.3: and understanding is in the sense of the act of understanding that.
vsm1.7:22.4: Hence it was said: ‘Understanding of discernment of conditions is knowledge of the causal relationship of states’” (Paṭis I 52).
vsm1.7:22.5: Thus when the Blessed One, by correctly knowing these states with knowledge of relations of states,
vsm1.7:22.6: became dispassionate towards them, when his greed faded away, when he was liberated,
vsm1.7:22.7: then he destroyed, quite destroyed, abolished, the spokes of this wheel of the round of rebirths of the kind just described.
vsm1.7:22.8: Because the spokes are thus destroyed he is accomplished (arahanta) also.
vsm1.7:22.9:
The spokes (ara) of rebirth’s wheel have been
Destroyed (hata) with wisdom’s weapon keen
vsm1.7:22.10:
By him, the Helper of the World,
And so “accomplished” (arahanta) he is called.
vsm1.7:23.1:
(iv) And he is worthy (arahati) of the requisites of robes, etc., and of the distinction of being accorded
homage because it is he who is most worthy of offerings.
vsm1.7:23.2: For when a Perfect One has arisen, important deities and human beings pay homage to none else;
vsm1.7:23.3: for Brahmā Sahampati paid homage to the Perfect One with a jewelled garland as big as Sineru,
vsm1.7:23.4: and other deities did so according to their means, as well as human beings as King Bimbisāra of Magadha and the king of Kosala.
vsm1.7:23.5: And after the Blessed One had finally attained Nibbāna,
vsm1.7:23.6: King Asoka renounced wealth to the amount of ninety-six million for his sake
vsm1.7:23.7: and founded eight-four thousand monasteries throughout all Jambudīpa (India).
vsm1.7:23.8: And so, with all these, what need to speak of others? Because of worthiness of requisites he is accomplished (arahanta) also.
vsm1.7:23.9:
So he is worthy, the Helper of the World,
Of homage paid with requisites;
vsm1.7:23.10:
the word
“Accomplished” (arahanta) has this meaning in the world:
Hence the Victor is worthy of that word.
vsm1.7:24.1:
(v) And he does not act like those fools in the world who vaunt their cleverness and yet
do evil, but in secret for fear of getting a bad name.
vsm1.7:24.2: Because of absence of secret (rahābhāva) evil-doing he is accomplished (arahanta) also.
vsm1.7:24.3:
No secret evil deed may claim
An author so august;
vsm1.7:24.4:
the name
“Accomplished” (arahanta) is his deservedly
By absence of such secrecy (rahābhāva).
vsm1.7:25.2:
The Sage of remoteness unalloyed,
Vanquished defiling foes deployed,
vsm1.7:25.3:
The spokes of rebirth’s wheel destroyed,
Worthy of requisites employed,
vsm1.7:25.4:
Secret evil he does avoid:
For these five reasons he may claim
This word “accomplished” for his name.
vsm1.7:26.1: He is fully enlightened (sammāsambuddha) because he has discovered (buddha) all things rightly (sammā) and by himself (sāmaṃ).
vsm1.7:26.2: In fact, all things were discovered by him rightly by himself in that he discovered,
vsm1.7:26.3: of the things to be directly known, that they must be directly known (that is, learning about the four truths),
vsm1.7:26.4: of the things to be fully understood that they must be fully understood (that is, penetration of suffering),
vsm1.7:26.5: of the things to be abandoned that they must be abandoned (that is, penetration of the origin of suffering),
vsm1.7:26.6: of the things to be realized that they must be realized (that is, penetration of the cessation of suffering),
vsm1.7:26.7: and of the things to be developed that they must be developed (that is, penetration of the path).
vsm1.7:26.9:
What must be directly known is directly known,
What has to be developed has been developed,
vsm1.7:26.10:
What has to be abandoned has been abandoned;
And that, brahman, is why I am enlightened (Sn 558).
vsm1.7:36.1: He is the knower of worlds because he has known the world in all ways.
vsm1.7:36.2:
For the Blessed One has experienced, known and penetrated the world in all ways to its individual
essence, its arising, its cessation, and the means to its cessation,
vsm1.7:36.3:
according as it is said: “Friend, that there is a world’s end where one neither
is born nor ages nor dies nor passes away nor reappears,
vsm1.7:36.4: which is to be known or seen or reached by travel—that I do not say.
vsm1.7:36.5: Yet I do not say that there is ending of suffering without reaching the world’s end.
vsm1.7:36.6: Rather, it is in this fathom-long carcass with its perceptions and its consciousness
vsm1.7:36.7:
that I make known the world, the arising of the world, the cessation of the world, and the way
leading to the cessation of the world.
vsm1.7:36.8:
“Tis utterly impossible
To reach by travel the world’s end;
vsm1.7:36.9:
But there is no escape from pain
Until the world’s end has been reached.
vsm1.7:36.11:
He is at peace who the world’s end has known
And hopes for neither this world nor the next” (S I 62).
vsm1.7:37.1: Moreover, there are three worlds: the world of formations, the world of beings, and the world of location.
vsm1.7:37.2: Herein, in the passage, “One world: all beings subsist by nutriment” (Paṭis I 122),
vsm1.7:37.3: the world of formations is to be understood.
vsm1.7:37.4: In the passage, “‘The world is eternal’ or ‘The world is not eternal’” (M I 426) it is the world of beings.
vsm1.7:37.5:
In the passage: “As far as moon and sun do circulate
Shining and lighting up the four directions,
vsm1.7:37.6:
Over a thousand times as great a world
Your power holds unquestionable sway” (M I 328)—
vsm1.7:37.7: it is the world of location.
vsm1.7:37.8: The Blessed One has known that in all ways too.
vsm1.7:38.1: Likewise, because of the words: “One world: all beings subsist by nutriment. Two worlds: mentality and materiality.
vsm1.7:38.2: Three worlds: three kinds of feeling. Four worlds: four kinds of nutriment.
vsm1.7:38.3: Five worlds: five aggregates as objects of clinging. Six worlds: six internal bases.
vsm1.7:38.4: Seven worlds: seven stations of consciousness. Eight worlds: eight worldly states.
vsm1.7:38.5: Nine worlds: nine abodes of beings. Ten worlds: ten bases.
vsm1.7:38.6: Twelve worlds: twelve bases. Eighteen worlds: eighteen elements” (Paṭis I 122),
vsm1.7:38.7: this world of formations was known to him in all ways.
vsm1.7:39.1: But he knows all beings’ habits, knows their inherent tendencies, knows their temperaments, knows their bents,
vsm1.7:39.2: knows them as with little dust on their eyes and with much dust on their eyes, with keen faculties and with dull faculties,
vsm1.7:39.3: with good behaviour and with bad behaviour, easy to teach and hard to teach, capable and incapable of achievement (cf. Paṭis I 121),
vsm1.7:39.4: therefore this world of beings was known to him in all ways.
vsm1.7:40.1: And as the world of beings so also the world of location.
vsm1.7:40.2:
For accordingly this world measures as follows: One world-sphere is twelve hundred thousand
leagues and thirty-four hundred and fifty leagues (1,203,450) in breadth and width.
vsm1.7:40.4:
The measure of it all around
Is six and thirty hundred thousand
vsm1.7:40.5:
And then ten thousand in addition,
Four hundred too less half a hundred (3,610,350).
vsm1.7:41.2:
Two times a hundred thousand leagues
And then four nahutas as well (240,000):
vsm1.7:41.3:
This earth, this “Bearer of All Wealth,”
Has that much thickness, as they tell.
vsm1.7:41.5:
Four times a hundred thousand leagues
And then eight nahutas as well (480,000):
vsm1.7:41.6:
The water resting on the air
Has that much thickness, as they tell.
vsm1.7:41.8:
Nine times a hundred thousand goes
The air out in the firmament
vsm1.7:41.9:
And sixty thousand more besides (960,000)
So this much is the world’s extent.
vsm1.7:42.1: Such is its extent. And these features are to be found in it:
vsm1.7:42.2:
Sineru, tallest of all mountains, plunges down into the sea
Full four and eighty thousand leagues, and towers up in like degree
vsm1.7:42.3:
Seven concentric mountain rings surround Sineru in suchwise
That each of them in depth and height is half its predecessor’s size:
vsm1.7:42.4:
Vast ranges called Yugandhara, Ìsadhara, Karavīka,
Sudassana, Nemindhara, Vinataka, Assakaṇṇa.
vsm1.7:42.5:
Heavenly breezes fan their cliffs agleam with gems, and here reside
The Four Kings of the Cardinal Points, and other gods and sprites beside.
vsm1.7:42.6: Himālaya’s lofty mountain mass rises in height five hundred leagues
vsm1.7:42.7: And in its width and in its breadth it covers quite three thousand leagues,
vsm1.7:42.8: And then it is bedecked besides with four and eighty thousand peaks.
vsm1.7:42.9:
The Jambu Tree called Nāga lends the name, by its magnificence,
To Jambudīpa’s land; its trunk, thrice five leagues in circumference,
Soars fifty leagues, and bears all round branches of equal amplitude,
So that a hundred leagues define diameter and altitude.
